annotation.speech2: On the left, the x y plane shows a point P 0 with coordinates x 0 y 0. A black arrow u d s leaves P 0 in the direction of the unit vector u, ending at the point P with coordinates x 0 plus u 1 d s, y 0 plus u 2 d s. Its horizontal component u 1 d s i is drawn in orange and its vertical component u 2 d s j in green. On the right, a horizontal z axis carries the two output values: f of x 0 y 0 in blue and f of the moved point in red. Two dashed gray arrows labeled f map P 0 and P to their output values, and the difference of the outputs is the change delta f.
The starting point P 0 with coordinates x 0, y 0.
The displacement u d s: moving away from P 0 a small distance d s in the direction of the unit vector u.
The horizontal component of the displacement, u 1 d s times i, drawn in orange.
The vertical component of the displacement, u 2 d s times j, drawn in green.
The point P reached after the displacement, with coordinates x 0 plus u 1 d s, y 0 plus u 2 d s.
The function f maps the starting point P 0 to the output value f of x 0 y 0, marked in blue on the z axis.
The function f maps the moved point P to the output value f of x 0 plus u 1 d s, y 0 plus u 2 d s, marked in red on the z axis.
The change in f, delta f, is the difference between the two output values on the z axis.
